summary: IEEE 802.1 defines Connectivity Fault Management, a set of tools for monitoring and troubleshooting Ethernet networks. It gave the IETF blocks of message opcodes and TLV types, and this document sets the rules IANA follows when handing out values from those blocks.

plainLanguage.summary: A big library gave the IETF a few shelves to fill with numbered books. This note explains who may put a new book on those shelves and how the numbers get picked.

questions: who assigns ethernet cfm tlv types
subtitle: IANA procedures for allocating Ethernet CFM message types and TLV codes from IEEE 802.1.

tldr.problem: IEEE 802.1 defined Connectivity Fault Management (CFM) for Ethernet network monitoring, and allocated blocks of message opcodes and TLV types to the IETF, but did not specify how IANA should manage assignments from those blocks.
tldr.mechanism: IANA creates registries for CFM OAM OpCodes and TLV Types, using Standards Action as the registration procedure for values 64-95 in each category.
tldr.outcome: The IANA registries enable the IETF to assign CFM message types and TLV extensions in a controlled and documented manner.

today: RFC 7319 is a Best Current Practice that remains in effect. IANA manages the CFM OpCode and TLV Type registries as specified, allowing the IETF to extend CFM functionality in a coordinated way.

sections.title: CFM and IANA Blocks
sections.content: IEEE 802.1 defined Connectivity Fault Management (CFM), a set of tools for monitoring and troubleshooting Ethernet networks. CFM messages have an OpCode field and support TLV-structured information. IEEE 802.1 allocated CFM OpCode block 64-95 and CFM TLV Type block 64-95 to the IETF for future use. This document specifies how IANA manages these allocations.
sections.plainLanguage: IEEE defined a network troubleshooting protocol and gave the IETF 32 slots for message types and 32 slots for data tags. Someone needed to explain who gets to use them.

sections.title: The Registries
sections.content: IANA maintains two registries under "Connectivity Fault Management (CFM) OAM IETF Parameters": the CFM OAM IETF OpCodes registry and the CFM OAM IETF TLV Types registry. Both use Standards Action as the registration procedure, meaning new assignments require approval by the IETF standards process. Values 64-95 in each registry are available for assignment; the registries reference both IEEE 802.1Q and RFC 7319.
sections.plainLanguage: Two numbered lists (one for opcodes, one for TLV types) start empty. To add to either list, you must go through the IETF standards process.

sections.title: Standards Action Requirement
sections.content: The requirement for Standards Action means that any new assignment from the CFM OpCode or TLV Type blocks allocated to the IETF must be approved through the formal IETF standards track process. This ensures coordinated allocation and prevents conflicts or duplicates. Earlier in the CFM protocol's history, IEEE 802.1 allocated a similar block of values 32-63 to the ITU-T for their own use, which now shows the division of responsibility between standards bodies.
sections.plainLanguage: Before IANA gives out a new number, the IETF has to formally agree it is needed. This keeps everyone organized.
